post.description:
Store a reference clip and get a `voice_id` to use in `POST /v1/speech` and
`POST /v1/speech/stream`. Nigerian-language voices are cloned by
**storm-gust**: the clip is checked first (it must hold at least 3 s of clear
speech, and STORM ASR 2.0 must be able to hear words in it). All other
languages are cloned by **storm-v3**, which also needs `reference_text`.
The clip is transcribed by STORM ASR 2.0, which detects the language itself, so
code-mixed speech is fine. Only clone a voice with the speaker's permission. Optionally,
to record that permission, have the speaker read the sentence from
`GET /v1/voices/consent` as the clip and send its `consent_prompt_id`: the voice is
marked `consent_verified` when the recording says it. Reading it is not required.

get.summary: Get a consent sentence to read
get.description:

`prompt_id` to send with the recording to `POST /v1/voices`. Valid for 30 minutes.

post.description:
Synthesize speech and return a WAV file.

Engine routing: Nigerian languages (`yo`, `ha`, `ig`, `pcm`, `en`) use
**storm-v1** with a built-in voice by default; a cloned `voice_id` uses the
engine it was created with; every other language uses **storm-v3**. Pass
`model` to pin an engine.

200.description: WAV audio. Headers: X-Request-ID, X-Model, X-Voice, X-Language, X-Characters, X-Cross-Lingual.

post.summary: Streaming text to speech (built-in and cloned voices)
post.description:
Stream audio as it is generated, for low time-to-first-sound, in the five
Nigerian languages. Streaming runs on **storm-gust** by default, built-in
and cloned voices alike; send `"mode": "quality"` (or pin `model`) to stream
a built-in voice on **storm-v1**. A take cannot be retried once audio has
started, so use `POST /v1/speech` when reliability matters more than latency.

200.description: Raw PCM, signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz. Headers: X-Audio-Format, X-Sample-Rate, X-Channels.

post.summary: Text to speech with a one-off reference clip
post.description:
Clone a voice from an uploaded clip for this one request, without saving it.
To reuse a voice, create it once with `POST /v1/voices` and pass its id to
`POST /v1/speech` instead.

200.description: WAV audio. Headers: X-Request-ID, X-Model, X-Voice, X-Language, X-Characters, X-Cross-Lingual.

post.description:
Speech to text with **STORM ASR 2.0** (Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin, Nigerian English and
code-mixed speech; no language needed). Audio longer than 15 s is split at pauses
and the pieces are transcribed separately, so long files come back complete
and there is no length limit beyond the upload cap.

For subtitles, captions or editing, ask for `timestamps=segment` (or a
subtitle file with `response_format=srt|vtt`): the audio is split at pauses
with voice activity detection, each piece is transcribed, and each comes
back with its start and end in seconds. Video files work too. Billed on the
audio's length either way.

Translate between any two of `en`, `yo`, `ha`, `ig`, `pcm` with **storm-mt**.
A pair with no English side (e.g. `yo` -> `ig`) is pivoted through English by
the engine; the response then carries `pivoted: true` and the intermediate
English text.

post.summary: Get the text of a web page or document
post.description:
Pull the readable text out of a web page, PDF, Word or text file, ready to
send to `POST /v1/speech`. Web pages give their main article text, without
menus or adverts. Send either `file` or `url`.

Nothing is billed: you pay only when the text is spoken. Up to 100,000
characters are returned (`truncated` says when a document was longer).
Scanned PDFs (pictures of pages) have no text layer; `warning` says when a
PDF looks partly scanned. Speech takes up to 5,000 characters per request,
so split longer text at paragraph ends.

ApiKey.name: X-API-Key
ApiKey.description: Your API key from the PlotWeaver dashboard (API Keys).

language.title: Language
language.description: Language the clip is spoken in

file.title: File
file.description: 5-10 s clean recording of one person speaking (wav/mp3/flac/m4a)

reference_text.title: Reference Text
reference_text.description: Transcript of the clip. Required for non-Nigerian languages (storm-v3).

consent_prompt_id.title: Consent Prompt Id
consent_prompt_id.description: Optional, from GET /v1/voices/consent. If the clip is the speaker reading that sentence, the voice is marked consent_verified; any other clip is still cloned, unverified.

rights_confirmed.title: Rights Confirmed
rights_confirmed.description: True confirms this is your own voice or you have the speaker's permission to clone it (Voice Cloning Policy). The app always sends it; it is stored on the voice.

file.title: File
file.description: A PDF, Word (.docx) or text file, up to 15 MB.

url.title: Url
url.description: A web page (article, blog post, news story) or a link to a PDF.

reference_audio.title: Reference Audio
reference_audio.description: 4-8 s clip of the voice to clone (wav/mp3)

reference_text.title: Reference Text
reference_text.description: Transcript of the clip. Required for storm-v3 (non-Nigerian languages).

file.title: File
file.description: Audio file (wav, mp3, m4a, ogg, flac...)

language.title: Language
language.description: Optional: `en`, `yo`, `ha`, `ig` or `pcm`. STORM ASR 2.0 recognises all five (and Yoruba-English code-mixing) without it.

timestamps.title: Timestamps
timestamps.description: `segment` adds `segments`: the transcript in timed pieces (start, end, text), cut at pauses.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: `srt` or `vtt` returns a subtitle file instead of JSON (implies timestamps=segment).

Bucket.title: Bucket
Bucket.description: One row of a breakdown: a product, service, model or language.

prompt_id.title: Prompt Id
prompt_id.description: Send with the recording to POST /v1/voices as consent_prompt_id.

text.title: Text
text.description: The sentence the speaker reads aloud, exactly as written.

KeyRow.title: KeyRow
KeyRow.description:
Usage by API key. `key_id` is None for calls made from the dashboard
(playground) and for keys that have since been deleted.

LanguageModelRow.title: LanguageModelRow
LanguageModelRow.description: Which model served which language, for which service.

text.title: Text
text.description: Text to speak. Normalised per language before synthesis (currency, numbers, units, times).

language.title: Language
language.description: Language code (e.g. `yo`, `ha`, `ig`, `pcm`, `en`, `sw`) or name. See GET /v1/languages.

voice_id.title: Voice Id
voice_id.description: A built-in voice id or name (see GET /v1/voices?language=xx, for example `tola`, `aderonke`, `maryam`) or the id of one of your cloned voices. Omit for the language's default voice.

model.description: Pin a TTS engine. Default: `storm-v1` for Nigerian languages, `storm-v3` otherwise. Cloned voices use the engine they were created with.

fast.title: Fast
fast.description: Skip the engine's quality-retry loop for lower latency.

normalize.title: Normalize
normalize.description: Apply Plotweaver text normalisation before synthesis.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: `quality`: built-in voices on storm-v1. `speed`: the same built-in voice on storm-gust, for the lowest latency (first audio in about 0.1 s when streaming), with a little less expression. Default: `quality` for POST /v1/speech, `speed` for POST /v1/speech/stream (unless `model` is pinned). Nigerian languages only; cloned voices always run on storm-gust.

TTSModel.title: TTSModel
TTSModel.description: Public names for the three TTS engines. Developers may pin one.

segments.title: Segments
segments.description: With timestamps=segment: the transcript in timed pieces, cut at pauses.

start.title: Start
start.description: Seconds from the start of the audio.

source_language.title: Source Language
source_language.description: Language code (e.g. `yo`, `ha`, `ig`, `pcm`, `en`, `sw`) or name. See GET /v1/languages.

target_language.title: Target Language
target_language.description: Language code (e.g. `yo`, `ha`, `ig`, `pcm`, `en`, `sw`) or name. See GET /v1/languages.
